findings.title: deleteCache mutation does not invalidate connectedCalendars query, leaving stale cache UI
findings.body: The `deleteCacheMutation` onSuccess only shows a toast and calls `onSuccess?.()` (the parent `onChanged` callback). It never invalidates `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars`, so the `cacheUpdatedAt` value that drives the "Cache Status" row and the "Delete cached data" item is not refetched. After a successful delete the dropdown still shows the old timestamp and offers the delete action again until the query happens to refetch. The sibling `disconnectMutation` correctly calls `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars.invalidate()` in onSettled; the delete-cache path should do the same.

findings.title: Instantiating CalendarCacheRepository directly bypasses the calendar-cache feature gate
findings.body: Everywhere else the cache layer is obtained via `CalendarCache.init(...)`, which returns `CalendarCacheRepositoryMock` when the `calendar-cache` feature is disabled. Here `new CalendarCacheRepository()` is constructed directly, so `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` always issues a `groupBy` query against `CalendarCache` on every `connectedCalendars` request, even for users/orgs that do not have calendar cache enabled. It also surfaces "cache status" for stale rows left over from when the feature was enabled. Use `CalendarCache.init(null)` so the feature flag is respected.

findings.title: Cache status ignores expiresAt, reporting expired cache as present
findings.body: `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` aggregates `_max(updatedAt)` over all rows for the credential, including rows whose `expiresAt` is in the past. `getCachedAvailability` only serves rows with `expiresAt >= now()`, so the UI can show a "Cache Status / Last updated" for data that is already expired and no longer used. If the intent is to show usable cache, the `where` clause should include `expiresAt: { gte: new Date() }`; otherwise the label is misleading.

findings.title: Cache timestamp hard-codes en-US locale
findings.body: The cache "last updated" timestamp is formatted with a hard-coded `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", ...)`. cal.com is localized (the component already uses `useLocale`), so users on other locales will always see a US-formatted date/time. It should use the current user's locale (e.g. from `useLocale`) rather than the literal "en-US".

findings.title: dev:cron switched to `npx tsx` but tsx is not a declared dependency
findings.body: The `dev:cron` script was changed from `ts-node cron-tester.ts` to `npx tsx cron-tester.ts`, but `tsx` is not listed in apps/web devDependencies (only `ts-node` is). `npx` will therefore try to download `tsx` on demand, making the script non-reproducible and liable to fail or prompt in offline/CI/restricted environments. This change is also unrelated to the calendar-cache feature and should either be reverted or accompanied by declaring `tsx` as a dependency.

findings.title: Dev script uses macOS-only sed syntax and a CWD-relative env path
findings.body: Two portability/correctness problems in the new helper script: (1) `sed -i '' -E ...` is BSD/macOS syntax; on GNU sed (Linux/CI) `-i ''` is parsed as an empty backup suffix and the command errors, so updating `GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL` fails. (2) `ENV_FILE="../.env"` is resolved relative to the current working directory, not the script location, so running `bash scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh` from the repo root writes/creates a `.env` in the parent of the repository instead of the repo's `.env`. Use a script-relative path and a portable sed invocation.

findings.title: New destructive mutation and cache-status query have no tests
findings.body: `deleteCacheHandler` performs an access-control check (credential must belong to `ctx.user`) and then deletes rows; `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` is a new query used to drive UI. Neither has any unit/integration test. Given this is a destructive, authorization-sensitive endpoint, at minimum there should be a test that a credentialId belonging to another user is rejected and that a valid delete removes exactly that credential's cache rows.
